newsitem.title: USA: USG to build $85 mln gypsum plant in Ohio.
newsitem.headline: USG to build $85 mln gypsum plant in Ohio.

text.p: USG Corp said Thursday its U.S. Gypsum Co subsidiary will invest about $85 million on a new plant in Gypsum, Ohio to manufacture gypsum wood fiber panels.
It said subsequent related projects could bring the total to $90 million.
Construction is scheduled to begin during the second quarter of 1997, and the facility is expected to begin production by the end of 1999.

"With gypsum wood fiber, USG is creating a new family of products that will extend its line of engineered construction panels, which includes Sheetrock brand gypsum wallboard and Durock cement board," said chairman William Foote.

The new operation will employ about 30 people at the outset and about 75 at full capacity. The company's current facility in Gypsum employs 305 people who manufacture Sheetrock brand gypsum wallboard.

Synthetic gypsum, one of the main raw materials to be used at the gypsum wood fiber facility, is a byproduct of several processes, including flue gas desulfurization (FGD). FGD removes sulfur dioxide from the emissions of fossil-fuel-burning power plants, thus reducing acid rain.
